questions.problem:
To prepare an orange perfume, Catherine must use $0.2$ liters of orange essence for each liter of alcohol. How much orange essence should Catherine use if she plans to use $0.6$ liters of alcohol?

Expressed as a decimal, Catherine must use
{{field-1}}
liters of the essence.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine the amount of orange essence that Catherine must mix with $0.6$ liters of alcohol, we must multiply $0.6$ by $0.2.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers.

Notice that the second number has a leading $0$, which we ignore during the multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.2\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in $0.6$ and there is $1$ decimal place in $0.2.$
Therefore, their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $12$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{12}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Hence, $0.6\times 0.2=0.12.$

We conclude that Catherine must use $0.12$ liters of the essence with $0.6$ liters of alcohol.

questions.problem:
Catherine mixes $3.4$ liters of alcohol with $0.68$ liters of orange essence. What is the volume of the mixture?

Expressed as a decimal, the volume of the mixture is
{{field-1}}
liters.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine the volume of the mixture, we need to calculate the sum $3.4+0.68.$

There is $1$ decimal place in $3.4$ and $2$ decimal places in $0.68.$

To add the numbers, they both need to have the same number of decimals. Hence, we rewrite the first number so that it has $2$ decimal places:

$$
3.4=3.40
$$

Next, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by adding the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the mixture is $4.08$ liters.

questions.problem:
Catherine used $9\,\frac{2}{7}$ liters of distilled water out of $10\,\frac{3}{4}$ liters of distilled water available. What is the volume of the remaining distilled water? Express your answer as a mixed number.

The volume of distilled water remaining equals$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\,$liters.
questions.worked_solution:
Caterine had $(10\,\frac{3}{4}-9\,\frac{2}{7})$ liters of distilled water left over.
 
Writing $10\,\frac{3}{4}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
10\,\frac{3}{4}=\frac{10\times 4+3}{4}=\frac{43}{4}.
$$

Writing $9\,\frac{2}{7}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
9\,\frac{2}{7}=\frac{9\times 7+2}{7}=\frac{65}{7}.
$$

Therefore, our problem now is to work out the following:

$$
\frac{43}{4}-\frac{65}{7}
$$

To subtract two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

In this question, we can make a common denominator of $28.$

To put $\frac{43}{4}$ over a denominator of $28,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$

$$
\frac{43}{4}=\frac{43\times 7}{4\times 7}=\frac{301}{28}
$$

To put $\frac{65}{7}$ over a denominator of $28,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$

$$
\frac{65}{7}=\frac{65\times 4}{7\times 4}=\frac{260}{28}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{301}{28}-\frac{260}{28}=\frac{41}{28}
$$

Finally, we convert back to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{41}{28}=1\,\text{R}\,13=1\,\frac{13}{28}
$$

Therefore, the volume of distilled water remaining equals $1\,\frac{13}{28}$ liters.

questions.problem:
Catherine sold $6$ identical bottles of perfume, for which she received a total of $$90.33.$ Estimate the price of each bottle by rounding the amount of money Catherine received to the nearest dollar.

The approximate price for each bottle is $
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To estimate the price of each of the $6$ perfumes, we need to find an approximation for $90.33÷6.$

So, we round the dividend to the nearest whole number:

$$
90.33\to 90
$$

Now, we divide $90$ by $6$ as usual:

$$
90÷6=15
$$

Therefore, the approximate price for each bottle is $$15.$
